description: A curated list of resources on event-driven architecture.

summary.what_it_does: This is an "awesome" style list of links rather than software. It is organized into Articles and Videos, each split into Foundational and Experience Reports and Practicalities subsections, plus a Related Topics section that points to event sourcing. Entries are short annotated descriptions with the author and date, and some note what is useful or where a talk's opening is skippable. The README says the list is deliberately highly curated and aims to cover principles and terminology. Contributions are accepted through issues or pull requests. The footer advertises the maintainer's consulting work, which is not part of the resource list.
use_cases: learn the basics of event-driven architecture
find talks on event-driven system design
read case studies of EDA at scale
compare orchestration and choreography in workflows
decide how to classify and size events
notable: Annotated entries with the author, date and the maintainer's own commentary on each resource
Covers the transactional outbox pattern, event granularity, event classification and orchestration vs. choreography
Includes experience reports from companies such as McDonald's, Michelin, Cinch and Investec
Explicitly curated and promotes principles and terminology over volume
caveats: Link list only; the linked content is not in the repository and may go stale
Contains personal opinions and critiques of individual talks
Footer promotes the maintainer's consulting services
